summary: The core has one module per custom chip (315-5211A, 5197, 5275, 5242, 5248/5249/5250, CXD1095), but those boundaries line up just as well with MAME's device classes, and the logic inside the video chips is MAME's C++ turned into state machines. The sprite renderer walks MAME's sega_outrun_sprite_device::draw loop step for step. The road generator copies segaic16_road_outrun_draw's priority_map and color_table. The mixer re-creates MAME's screen_update draw order and its priority-bitmap values. A few pieces depart from MAME the way the board would, mainly the sub-bus arbiter and the conditional framebuffer swap with abort at vblank, but they are a small share of the board-specific logic.

findings.note: R_DECODE pulls out hide/bank/top/pitch/xpos/vzoom/hzoom/height/colpri with MAME's exact masks, including bank %= numbanks and the 0x40 zoom clamp. R_PIX is MAME's 'for k<8 { while (xacc<0x200) {...; xacc+=hzoom} xacc-=0x200; pixels>>=4 }' loop turned into a state machine.

findings.signal: MAME heuristics carried into the sprite engine
findings.note: Copies MAME's nibble-reversal swizzle for non-flipped data, the 'xpos < 0x80 && xdelta < 0 then +0x200' adjustment that MAME itself calls a guessed threshold, and MAME's last_data test (pixels & 0x0f000000) == 0x0f000000 for end of row.

findings.signal: sprite row stepping uses MAME's data[7]/addr scheme
findings.note: rowaddr/addr act as MAME's data[7] working pointer and row base. next_row does MAME's 'yacc += vzoom; addr += pitch*(yacc>>9); yacc &= 0x1ff', and off-screen rows are skipped the same way MAME's cliprect test skips them.

pmap() holds MAME's priority_map[2][8] constants (0x80,0x81,0x87,0x8f...) and ct00..ct17 are MAME's color_table entries (colorbase1 ^ 0x02 ^ color bit, ...). HOFF folds in MAME's (0x5f8 + xoffs) with MAME's X Board xoffs of -166. The board would do this with a PROM or gate logic, not this table form.

The combinational block applies the layers in MAME's tilemap_draw call order (road bg, road fg if prio 0, bg pri0/1, fg pri0/1, road fg if prio 1, text) and builds a 'mark' from MAME's priority-bitmap values 0x01/0x02/0x02/0x04/0x04/0x08. The sprite rule '(1<<prio) > mark' and the (pix & 0x400f)==0x400a shadow test are taken from MAME. That is a priority-bitmap model, not the 315-5279 PAL logic.

Scroll and page selection is MAME's: effxscroll = (xscroll&0x8000 ? rowscroll : xscroll), rowscroll bit 15 picks set which+2, effx = (0xc0 - xs) & 0x3ff, and column scroll reads textram[0xf16/2 + (x+8)/16] (0x78B). The values are latched at line 261, which is MAME's latch timer, through tilemap_16b_fill_latch's registers.

The IPL encoding (timer=2, vblank=4, both=6) is MAME's 'irq |= 2; irq |= 4'. The GP Rider clamp to 4 copies m_gprider_hack, and the watchdog is kicked by vblank, which is MAME's write_line_ck in the same function. A game-specific Thunder Blade sprite-RAM wipe hack is also carried over (xb_core.sv:298).

findings.signal: math/compare chips modeled on MAME register arrays
findings.note: The 5250 uses registers r0..r7 with MAME's read mirrors (5 to r1, 6 to r2), MAME's history bit counter and the 'old_counter == 0xfff fires regardless of enable' rule. The divider's overflow path computes the remainder from the clamped quotient the way MAME does, though the division engine itself is a restoring divider.

findings.signal: sub-bus arbitration MAME does not model
findings.mame_ref: src/mame/sega/segaxbd.cpp:main_map (0x200000-0x27ffff mapped straight to subcpu ROM)
findings.note: Main CPU accesses to the sub space take the sub bus through an arbiter that defers and replays sub CPU cycle starts, withholding DTACK from the sub CPU. MAME maps the sub space directly into the main CPU's map with no contention.

findings.signal: framebuffer render abort and conditional swap
findings.mame_ref: src/mame/sega/sega16sp.cpp:sega_outrun_sprite_device::draw (redrawn every frame from the buffered list)
findings.note: A render is started by the $110000 write and cut off at vblank, and the buffers swap only if a render ran. That is a chip-style sequencer behaviour that differs from MAME's every-frame batch redraw, though the drawing it sequences is still MAME's loop.

findings.where: rtl/video/xb_sprite_5211.sv, xb_tilemap_5197.sv, xb_road_5275.sv, xb_palette_5242.sv, rtl/cpu/xb_math_5248.sv, xb_math_5249.sv, xb_cmptimer_5250.sv, rtl/io/xb_cxd1095.sv
findings.note: The modules are named after the board's chips, but each matches a MAME device class with the same register interface, and the ports are bus-style cs/we/addr rather than chip pins. It does not separate the two hypotheses.

The tilemap and road render the next line into double-buffered BRAM line buffers, one or two clocks per pixel, driven by the raster counter. That is ordinary FPGA engineering, while the per-pixel computation inside is MAME's.
